data.raw_text:
Geopolitics tests the truce as live fire, frozen funds and China’s rare-earth squeeze keep markets on edge, despite ceasefire extension plans.

• US-Iran: White House/US military officials labelled Iran’s overnight strike toward a US airbase via Kuwait an “egregious ceasefire violation,” while CNN analysis says Tehran is actively staging a broader missile arsenal.

• Direct clashes: US CENTCOM launched defensive air strikes near Bandar Abbas after detecting an imminent drone threat, downing four Iranian drones and destroying a ground control station.

• Retaliation: Iran’s IRGC responded around 04:50 local time with strikes on a US-linked airbase and warned of a “more decisive” response.

• Hormuz: Iranian state media said the IRGC navy fired live warning shots at four commercial cargo ships near the Strait after accusing them of transiting without coordination.

• Oman warning: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly warned Oman and other regional partners they could face penalties if they help Iran collect Strait transit tolls.

• 60-day track: despite live fire, Washington and Tehran reportedly have a 60-day temporary truce outline including nuclear talks, but it still awaits Trump approval and remains unstable.

• Nuclear condition: The same outline reportedly includes an Iranian pledge not to build a nuclear weapon during the 60-day freeze in exchange for Washington unfreezing billions in trapped global assets.

• Tehran demands: Iran added a major financial condition, demanding the return of billions in frozen global funds before signing any 60-day truce.

• Israel-Gaza/Lebanon: Israel carried out a targeted campaign that reportedly eliminated Hamas’s newly appointed military chief Muhammad Od plus other commanders, while Lebanon/Gaza ceasefire pressure keeps unraveling.

• Lebanon escalation: The geographic expansion is now moving beyond the Litani line toward the Zahrani River, with Israeli operations reportedly widening the effective combat zone deeper into southern Lebanon.

• US-Ukraine: Zelensky sent a formal letter directly to Trump appreciating support and requesting Patriot air-defense munitions.

• Ukraine-Russia: Ukraine showed European ambassadors recovered Oreshnik missile components, including Belarus-linked electronics, and analysts flagged one failed Oreshnik launch as a 25% failure rate across four known launches.

• US-Canada trade: Mark Carney warned the global trading system is undergoing a permanent “rupture,” calling for a tighter US-Canada partnership around aluminum, autos and critical minerals.

• Indo-Pacific: China said it forcibly drove away a Dutch naval frigate in the South China Sea, while Western focus remains heavily on Hormuz.

• Japan-Philippines: Japan and the Philippines launched talks for a GSOMIA intelligence-sharing pact to coordinate maritime responses against China’s gray-zone pressure.

• Rare earths: China’s rare-earth squeeze on Japan deepened, with medium/heavy rare earths and permanent magnets reportedly nearly halted, threatening Japan’s auto, tech, EV, semiconductor and missile-guidance supply chains.

• China-Japan rhetoric: Beijing accused Tokyo of “neo-militarism,” citing defense-budget hikes, Type-12 stand-off missiles and constitutional-security shifts.

• Decoupling race: Japanese manufacturers like TDK and Mitsubishi are searching for alternatives via Australia/France supply chains, but replacing heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium could take years.

• DRC crisis: WHO warned of a catastrophic war-and-disease collision in the DRC, while Uganda sealed its border after Ebola cases reportedly surged.

This is no longer just “deal or no deal.”

The market is now trading a negotiation surrounded by weapons, choke points, sanctions, supply chains, and political deadlines.

So the real question is: does the 60-day outline cool the system down, or does every new “condition” just create another trigger for the next shock?
